subject: SCIENCE
title: Pushes and Pulls
introduction: Milo pushes a toy cart and pulls open a drawer. What makes things move — or stop moving?

vocabulary.definition: A push or a pull on something.
To move something away from you.
To bring something closer to you.

items.prompt: Which statement about forces is true?

options.text: A force is a push or pull; changes in motion depend on combined forces and constraints.

items.explanation: A force is a push or a pull. Whether something moves depends on the forces acting on it — a push does not always make it move.

options.text: let a ball roll on its own

items.explanation: Pushing sends the toy cart away from you. Pulling brings a drawer toward you, and a rolling ball is not being pushed.

items.prompt: Which statement about forces is NOT true?
items.explanation: A force does not always make something move — a heavy box can stay still even when pushed. Pushing a cart and pulling a drawer are real forces.

items.prompt: Opening a drawer toward you is mainly a
items.explanation: You bring the drawer toward you, and pulling means bringing something closer. Color and sound are not forces.

items.prompt: Which statement about forces and motion is true?

options.text: a push always makes things fly

items.explanation: Friction rubs against moving things and slows them down. A push does not always make things fly, and forces can start motion too.
